newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-FINLEY HITS THREE HOMERS AS PADRES POUND REDS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-FINLEY HITS THREE HOMERS AS PADRES POUND REDS.

text.p: Steve Finley helped the San Diego Padres enjoy a rather extraordinary day Monday.
Finley belted three of San Diego's club record-tying five home runs and the Padres recorded their first triple play in eight years in a 13-6 rout of the Cincinnati Reds.
All of Finley's homers were solo blasts. He connected in the third and fourth innings off loser Pete Schourek for a 5-2 lead, and in the ninth off Stan Belinda to cap the scoring.
Finley's final blast followed a home run by pinch hitter Carlos Hernandez. Terry Shumpert hit a two-run homer in the fourth off Schourek.
"I've done it in three straight at-bats but never three in the same game," said Finley, who had homered twice in a game on three occasions.

Schourek (2-4) allowed six runs and six hits in just 4 1/3 innings. Will Cunnane (2-1) pitched four scoreless innings to earn the win. Starter Andy Ashby left in the second with a strained right elbow.

The day also featured the Padres' first triple play since April 9, 1989. With the bases loaded, Eddie Taubensee of the Reds lined to Ashby, who threw to Chris Gomez at shortstop to get Curtis Goodwin. Gomez then fired to first baseman Archi Cianfroccco to end the inning.
"We got breaks all over the place," said Padres right fielder Tony Gwynn. "We'll take it."
In Atlanta, Denny Neagle won his seventh consecutive game and Chipper Jones homered and drove in four runs and as the Braves completed a four-game sweep of the St Louis Cardinals with a 7-3 victory.
Neagle allowed two runs and five hits over six innings to improve to a perfect 7-0, tying for the league lead for wins.

Jones belted a three-run homer off Cardinals starter Todd Stottlemyre (2-3) over the left-centre field wall in the first inning. After St. Louis rallied for two runs, Jones doubled home Michael Tucker in the bottom of the sixth for a 4-2 lead as Stottleymyre was foiled in a bid for his 100th career win.
In New York, John Olerud's two-run homer with one out in the bottom of the ninth inning lifted the Mets to a 4-3 victory over the Colorado Rockies.
Olerud rescued starter Armando Reynoso, who took a no-hitter into seventh but nearly lost after giving up a two-run single to Andres Galarraga in the eighth for a 3-2 Rockies lead.
Reynoso faced just three batters over the minimum until Jeff Reed homered with two out in the seventh. Cory Lidle (2-0) pitched a scoreless ninth for the win.
Jeff McCurry (1-1) started the ninth for Colorado and gave up a double to Edgardo Alfonzo before Olerud drove the first pitch over the wall in right-centre.
In Chicago, Scott Servais delivered five RBI and Mark Grace and Shawon Dunston added two apiece as the Cubs pounded out 18 hits in a 15-4 thrashing of the San Francisco Giants.

Steve Trachsel (2-4) allowed three runs and nine hits in seven innings for Chicago for his first win since April 29. San Francisco's Osvaldo Fernandez (3-4) was tagged for six runs and eight hits in three innings.
Servais's three-run homer in the sixth off Rene Arocha gave the Cubs a 13-1 lead as Chicago scored in every inning but the fifth and eighth.
In Montreal, Jeff Juden pitched eight scoreless innings and the Expos scratched out two runs for a 2-1 victory over the Los Angeles Dodgers and their seventh win in eight games.
Juden (4-0) allowed just five hits before Todd Zeile led off the ninth with a homer for the Dodgers. Ramon Martinez (3-3) was reached for two runs and five hits over six innings.
Montreal scored on a passed ball in the fifth and picked up a run in the sixth when Rondell White scored on a sacrifice fly by Henry Rodriguez after doubling and stealing third.
In Philadelphia, Darryl Kile allowed one run and six hits over seven innings and Jeff Bagwell homered twice to lead the Houston Astros to a 9-5 win over the Phillies.
Kile (4-2) walked two and struck out eight. He has given up just two runs in his last four starts, spanning 31 innings.
Houston led 9-1 when John Hudek surrendered a three-run homer to Rico Brogna, who also homered off Kile in the sixth. Billy Wagner gave up a homer to Kevin Jordan in the ninth.
Sean Berry and Craig Biggio homered off Calvin Maduro (3-5) to help stake the Astros to a 4-0 lead. Houston put away the game with four more runs in the sixth.
